Timeline::numel¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

std::int64_t Timeline::numel() const

What It Tells You¶

numel() returns the number of logical timestamp positions, equal to the product of all entries in sizes(). It counts positions, including positions that hold NaT; it does not count only valid timestamps.

A scalar contains one position, so its count is 1 even though its shape is empty. If any shape extent is zero, the product and therefore the element count is zero.

This is the right query for allocation sizing, flat export lengths, loops over all positions, and emptiness tests. It does not tell you rank or how values are arranged.

Returns¶

The logical number of positions as std::int64_t.

Examples¶

Example 1. Compare rank and cardinality across common shapes.

auto scalar = pluss::timeline::make("2024-02-29T12:30:00Z");
auto matrix = pluss::timeline::make({
    {"2024-02-29T12:30:00Z", "2024-03-01T00:00:00Z"},
    {"2024-03-02T06:15:00Z", ""},
});

std::cout << "scalar: dim=" << scalar.dim()
          << ", numel=" << scalar.numel() << "\n"
          << "matrix: dim=" << matrix.dim()
          << ", numel=" << matrix.numel() << "\n";

Output¶

scalar: dim=0, numel=1
matrix: dim=2, numel=4

The matrix count is four even though one position is NaT: missingness is a value property, not an absent array slot.

Example 2. Test emptiness by cardinality.

auto empty = pluss::timeline::epoch({2, 0, 4});
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "dim=" << empty.dim()
          << ", numel=" << empty.numel()
          << ", empty=" << (empty.numel() == 0) << "\n";

Output¶

dim=3, numel=0, empty=true

Example 3. Flat epoch export has exactly numel() entries.

auto times = pluss::timeline::epoch({2, 3});
auto ticks = times.ticks();
std::cout << "numel=" << times.numel()
          << ", exported=" << ticks.size() << "\n";

Output¶

numel=6, exported=6

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • numel() == 1 does not prove that the timeline is scalar. Shapes [1] and [1, 1] also contain one position.

  • NaT contributes one to numel() like every other stored timestamp.

  • numel() is not a byte count. Epoch export stores each position as one std::int64_t.

  • Use numel() == 0, not dim() == 0, to test emptiness.
